A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GFM-RAG. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added material in v2.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix D report original retrieval, question-answering, generalization, ablation and scaling experiments.

after.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix E retain original experimental results and add baseline comparisons, knowledge-graph completion results and further controlled analyses.

M1.justification: The query-dependent GNN, two-stage training, BCE/ranking objective and top-20 entity-based document ranking remain unchanged. Renaming unsupervised pre-training as self-supervised pre-training and evaluating component variants do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The same three multi-hop QA and seven domain-specific RAG corpora remain. v2 additionally evaluates knowledge-graph completion on HotpotQA's test KG-index (Appendix E.2, Table 11), extending evaluation beyond v1's retrieval/QA outcomes. Knowledge-graph completion was already used for pre-training.

E2.justification: v2 adds GraphRAG (MS), SubgraphRAG, G-retriever, Adaptive-RAG and FLARE to the retrieval comparison. GraphRAG (MS), Adaptive-RAG and FLARE also enter the QA comparison, while LightRAG enters the latency comparison. Table 9 additionally compares GFM-RAG with standalone pre-trained and fine-tuned sentence embeddings.

E3.justification: The original main experimental settings remain, but added studies introduce substantial evaluation controls: KGC evaluation using MRR and Hits@1/3/10, four ranking variants, separate training on each QA dataset, GNN depths of 1/2/4/6/8 at hidden dimension 512, and comparisons using GPT-4o-mini versus GPT-3.5-turbo graph construction.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds analyses isolating the GNN's contribution beyond sentence embeddings, testing training strategies on KGC, comparing document-ranking components, evaluating transfer from individual training datasets, varying GNN depth and testing sensitivity to the graph-construction LLM. The earlier embedding-choice, loss-weight, transfer, scaling and reasoning-path analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2's checklist item 7 newly states that experiments use a fixed random seed and report no error bars. v1 provides no corresponding seed disclosure. This adds reporting information without establishing additional runs or introducing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained headline retrieval and QA scores are unchanged; GFM-RAG's R@5 remains 87.1, 58.2 and 95.6 across the three QA datasets. v2 substantially expands reported baseline, ablation, transfer, depth and construction-cost results. For example, new Table 11 reports KGC MRR of 0.304 with pre-training only, 0.193 with both stages and 0.029 without KGC pre-training.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematical formulations are retained. New Appendix A explains query-dependent GNN reasoning through an illustrative logical rule and references to prior theoretical work; it introduces no new formal definition, assumption, theorem, proof or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the claims of an 8M-parameter graph foundation retriever enabling single-step multi-hop retrieval, generalization to unseen datasets, strong performance and scaling behavior. The added domain-specific qualification to fine-tuning clarifies the existing generalization claim.

C2.justification: Where v1 emphasizes pre-training as crucial, v2 acknowledges its small effect on final retrieval and argues for its broader graph-reasoning role using KGC results. v2 also adds interpretations concerning GNN depth, ranking design and graph-quality robustness, alongside explicit indexing-cost and evaluation-scope limitations in Appendix G.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the OpenIE prompt in Appendix F/Table 22, adds construction cost/time information and expands training and data-split explanations. Existing hyperparameters, hardware and training budgets remain. The front-matter access instruction changes from a direct code-repository link to a project-page link.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Adaptive-RAG, SubgraphRAG, HOLMES, GraphGPT, HiGPT and additional GNN reasoning literature, while removing the Identity-aware GNN reference. It explicitly contrasts GNN-based GFMs with transformer-style models on graph scale and logical associations, while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: Main Sections 1–5 and most existing prose retain their organization and wording. v2 refines training terminology, expands explanatory examples, updates author information, adds acknowledgments and a checklist, and extends the appendix organization. The impact statement moves into the appendix.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column NeurIPS layout, with extensive resizing and repositioning of figures and tables. Training statistics move into the appendix, comparison tables gain rows, and new analysis and prompt tables are added. All six original figures are retained with placement, sizing or labeling changes.

improvement.justification: The expanded baseline comparisons and targeted GNN, ranking, transfer and graph-builder controls better support and qualify the method's advantages. Explicit limitations and the OpenIE prompt improve transparency. These gains are tempered by new cost inconsistencies between Appendix E.9 and Tables 18–19, and an overstated robustness interpretation: Table 21 shows higher GFM-RAG scores under both builders, but larger R@5 decreases between builders than HippoRAG.
